sourceEvidence.title: Sr Staff Systems Engineer
sourceEvidence.quote:
The Producibility Architect will be located in our Gilbert, AZ facility, and will report to the OU Office of the Chief Engineer and OU Profit and Loss leaders. Specific duties include, but are not limited to:
* Maintaining product lessons learned databases, establishing actionable plans for implementation of process enhancements to incorporate lessons learned, collaborating across the engineering, manufacturing and AI&T teams to ensure plans are executed and maintaining metrics that capture quantitative measures of enhancement effectiveness
* Working with systems engineering and AI&T teams to identify opportunities for testing automation based on cost-benefit analysis and developing detailed roadmaps for implementing the automation
* Collaborating with Mission Assurance and Systems Engineering Functional Groups to develop detailed mission risk classification tailoring plans for OU products, based on Government standards, and performing as the liaison to customer engineering leadership to help ensure our approach meets customer mission risk classification needs per our contracts
* Working with NG Division, Sector and Corporate groups to explore use of AI/ML across the development lifecycle of our OU products in order to reduce touch labor and shorten production timelines
* Coordinating with manufacturing work centers to execute value stream mapping events and internal audits to enhance producibility
* Audit of OU program processes with focus on streamlined execution, culminating with functional and mission assurance leadership to codify approved, rapid development and manufacturing processes for OU products
* Independent reviewer of OU program system engineering processes, supporting appropriate tailoring of program System Engineering Management Plans (SEMPs) to facilitate rapid design cycles and more efficient verification and validation of products.
**
Basic Requirements:**
* Bachelor’s degree in a STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Math) discipline with 14+ years of engineering experience, or Master’s degree in a STEM discipline with 12+ years of engineering experience
* Full lifecycle Systems Engineering experience as applied to spacecraft development
* Experience with spacecraft subsystem design and test
* Familiarity with Government Mission Risk Classification processes and their application to space systems
* Experienced technical leader with proven capabilities to support complex, constrained program execution in short timelines
* **Active or current U.S. Government Top Secret security clearance**
